results.controlIntent: (a) Set up and administer privileged user accounts in accordance with [Selection: a role-based access scheme; an attribute-based access scheme]; (b) Monitor assignments of privileged roles or attributes; (c) Monitor changes to roles or attributes; and (d) Revoke access when privileged role or attribute assignments are no longer appropriate.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from both the IAM execution role and CloudTrail events reveals multiple failures across all four sub-requirements of AC-2(7).v1:

**(a) Role-based/attribute-based scheme:** The endpoint's execution role (`SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic`, ARN: `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic`) carries two wildcard policies — `s3:*` on `*` and `sagemaker:*` on `*`. These are not scoped to specific resources, actions, or roles, violating the principle of least-privilege that underpins a proper role-based access scheme. The "Generic" naming also signals the role is not purpose-built for this endpoint.

**(b) Monitor privileged role assignments:** No evidence of monitoring for privileged role assignments was found. The overly broad policies were granted without apparent review or scoping, and there is no indication of a process to detect or alert on inappropriate privilege grants.

**(c) Monitor changes to roles/attributes:** Two CloudTrail events reveal uncontrolled changes. `CreateEndpoint` (2025-12-01T11:00:00Z) was executed by `data-scientist-jdoe` approximately 2 hours *before* registry approval (noted at 09:00), meaning the deployment bypassed the change-control gate. `UpdateEndpoint` (2026-03-15T14:22:00Z), also by `data-scientist-jdoe`, applied a hotfix with no corresponding registry entry at all. These events indicate that changes to privileged endpoint configurations are not being monitored or gated effectively.

**(d) Revoke access when no longer appropriate:** No evidence of access revocation processes or lifecycle management was found. The persistent wildcard permissions and the ability of a single IAM user to deploy and update endpoints without registry approval suggest that access is not being reviewed or revoked when circumstances change.

In summary, the role is over-privileged and not properly scoped, deployments are occurring outside of approved change-control processes, and there is no observable monitoring or revocation mechanism in place.
gaps: No IAM Access Analyzer or AWS Config rule evidence was available to assess ongoing monitoring of role assignments and policy changes.
No evidence of a formal access review or recertification process (e.g., quarterly reviews) for the SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic role.
No evidence of alerting/SIEM integration for CloudTrail events related to privileged SageMaker or S3 actions.
No evidence of a role revocation or offboarding process for data-scientist-jdoe or similar privileged users.
Registry approval timestamps were referenced in CloudTrail notes but the registry system itself was not directly queried — human attestation of the approval workflow would strengthen this finding.

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped

payload.note: Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00 — change control not satisfied
